THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: ÖÖD fits UNDERFLOOR HEATING as standard, beneath natural stone ceramic tiles, and states that it 'ensures warmth in the coldest winters'. That makes it the third supplier in this layer to include heating — after Sprout Pod and Luxury Garden Studios — and the only one to fit underfloor heating rather than a panel heater or an air-conditioning unit. Underfloor heating suits a highly glazed building because it warms surfaces and occupants rather than air, which stratifies and is lost at glass. THE STRUCTURAL POSITION, which has to be stated plainly: these are STEEL-FRAMED, MIRROR-GLASS-WALLED buildings. Glass loses heat several times faster than an insulated opaque wall no matter how good the unit, and a steel frame conducts heat around whatever insulation exists. ÖÖD publishes 'high-quality insulation' as a phrase and gives NO material, NO thickness, NO U-value and — most significantly — NO GLAZING SPECIFICATION. It is not stated anywhere in the available evidence whether the mirror glass is double or triple glazed, argon filled or low-E coated. Every other insulated supplier in this layer at least names its glazing. On a building whose defining feature is that its walls are glass, that is the one number a buyer cannot do without, and it is the one that is missing. WHAT IS PUBLISHED AND IS GENUINE: 97 per cent UV reflection is a real performance figure and it addresses summer overheating, which is the other half of the problem in a glass building. It says nothing about winter heat loss. MARKET POSITION recorded as intelligence: ÖÖD is an Estonian manufacturer whose stated market is nature hospitality — short-stay and glamping accommodation — rather than domestic garden offices, and several models are named accordingly.
